_about: Fractal Challenge course for Dojo. Five missions, ported from github.com/minka-iyer/fractal-challenge (levels.js) into Dojo's own PaperLang: the turtle starts facing right, inputs are plain names (def grow size do), and Dojo's 'when' takes the place of if/else. Read by DojoWeb.FractalLive (copy) and by the browser hook (solution, for the ghost and the check). Optional per-level tolerance overrides the checker default (the circle is stricter so a hexagon does not count). No em dashes in copy.

def.name: Make your own
def.example:
def grow size do
  fw size
end
def.label: def grow size do ... end

when.name: Only when
when.example:
when size < 20 do
  fw size
end
when.label: when size < 20 do ... end

levels.title: Draw a triangle
levels.goal: Make the turtle draw a triangle with three equal sides. Trace the faint shape.
levels.solution:
fw 100
rt 120
fw 100
rt 120
fw 100
rt 120
hints: The turtle starts facing right. Start with a line: `fw 100`.
After each side the turtle has to turn before it draws the next one. Try `rt` after `fw 100`.
The outside turns of a closed shape add up to 360. Three corners: `fw 100`, then `rt` a third of 360, and repeat.

options: Three turns have to add up to one full circle, and 360 / 3 = 120.
rt 60 would work too, it just looks smaller.
quiz.why: The turtle turns a full 360 by the time it gets back to the start. Split between 3 corners, that is 120 each.

levels.title: Draw a hexagon
levels.goal: Six equal sides. Can you do it without typing fw six times?
hints: Six equal sides means doing the same two things six times. `loop 6 do ... end` repeats what is inside.
Inside the loop: one line of `fw 100` and one turn. Do not forget `end`.
Six turns must add up to 360. So each turn is 360 / 6. Write `rt` with that number.

quiz.q: Why does a hexagon use rt 60 inside loop 6?
options: 6 turns of 60 make 360, one full turn.
Because 60 is the length of each side.
Any angle works as long as the loop is 6.
quiz.why: To close the shape, the turns must add up to a full 360. 6 x 60 = 360.

levels.title: Draw a circle
levels.goal: The turtle can only move in straight lines. How do you make something round?
hints: A circle is a shape with a lot of very short sides. Use a loop with a big number, like `loop 36 do`.
Make each step short and each turn small. Try `fw 10` and a small `rt`.
Turns must add up to 360. If you loop 36 times, each turn is 360 / 36. Write `rt` with that.

quiz.q: Why do short steps and small turns look like a circle?
options: The sides get so short that the corners look smooth.
The turtle switches to curved lines.
quiz.why: More sides means shorter sides and smaller corners. With enough of them, your eyes see a curve.

levels.title: Draw a spiral
levels.goal: Each line is a little longer than the one before. Make your own command that moves a bit further every time.
levels.solution:
def grow size do
  fw size
  rt 90
end

grow 20
grow 40
grow 60
grow 80
grow 100
grow 120
grow 140
grow 160
hints: Make your own command with an input: `def grow size do ... end`. The input `size` is a number you pass in.
Inside, use `size` like a number: `fw size`, then a quarter turn. Call it like `grow 20`.
Now call `grow` again with a bigger number each time: `grow 20`, `grow 40`, `grow 60`, and keep going up to `grow 160`.

quiz.q: What changes each time you call your command?
options: The number you give it, which sets how far to go.
Nothing. The turtle just goes in circles.
quiz.why: The input `size` holds the number you give, so one command can draw short and long lines.

levels.title: Draw a snowflake fractal
levels.goal: Every edge has a bump. Every bump has smaller bumps. Write a command that uses itself.
levels.solution:
def edge size do
  when size < 25 do
    fw size
  end
  when size >= 25 do
    edge size/3
    lt 60
    edge size/3
    rt 120
    edge size/3
    lt 60
    edge size/3
  end
end

loop 3 do
  edge 180
  rt 120
end
hints: Start with a triangle made of three `edge` calls: `loop 3 do`, then `edge 180` and `rt 120`, then `end`. Then teach `edge` how to draw itself.
A bumpy edge is four smaller edges, each a third as long: edge, `lt 60`, edge, `rt 120`, edge, `lt 60`, edge. Write each one as `edge size/3`.
When the edge is short, just draw a line, or it never stops. Use `when size < 25 do fw size end`, and put the four smaller edges inside `when size >= 25 do ... end`.

quiz.q: What stops edge from calling itself forever?
options: When the size is small, it draws a plain line instead.
The computer gets tired and stops.
The `end` at the bottom of the command.
quiz.why: A command that calls itself needs a way to stop. Here, the first `when` draws a plain line once `size` is small enough.
